title: Kinetic energy and momentum
hook: Change kinetic energy and predict momentum magnitude.
misconception: momentum magnitude doubles when kinetic energy doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply p = √(2mK) to compare momentum magnitude when kinetic energy changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a nonrelativistic particle of fixed mass, p = √(2mK). When kinetic energy doubles, momentum magnitude becomes √2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model p = √(2mK); scaling exponent 0.5. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a nonrelativistic particle of fixed mass, with a nonzero initial result. If kinetic energy triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on momentum magnitude?
recall.why: Apply p = √(2mK) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is √3.
